newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge union breaks off talks -report.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge union breaks off talks -report.

text.p: Contract talks between Falconbridge Ltd and the union representing more than 1,400 of the nickel miner's Sudbury workers broke down on Wednesday after the union angrily left the bargaining table, the Canadian Press reported.
CP said the Canadian Auto Workers union broke off talks Wednesday afternoon after claiming the company has not bargained honestly.

"The last couple of days we were able to determine that the company has been operating under an umbrella of deceit," union spokesman Rolly Gauthier told the news agency. "That's caused a complete collapse on the integrity of the bargaining processes."
Earlier this month, Falconbridge's 1,400 unionized mine workers in Sudbury voted 91.28 percent in favor of giving their negotiating team a strike mandate.
The current contract expires at the end of July.
Gauthier said he is worried there may not be enough time left to resolve outstanding issues, including wages, benefits and shift scheduling, without a walkout, CP reported.

"With the amount of work that we have remaining, it would require an enormous amount of effort to be able to reach any collective agreement by August 1...Quite frankly, I don't believe that we have the time," Gauther said.
Earlier today Falconbridge director of human resources Gerald Foley told Reuters talks were still on track and a deal could be reached before the strike deadline.
"They pay me to be an optimist and I still believe it (an agreement before August 1) will happen," Foley told Reuters.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations produced 42,100 tonnes of nickel, 48,800 tonnes of copper and 730 tonnes of cobalt last year.
